user.title: Second Brain
user.description: Persistent markdown knowledge store for your voice assistant. The chosen folder is used directly as the store - markdown files are created inside it. Leave LLM fields empty to disable the consolidator; everything here can be changed later under Configure.

data.core_chars: Max chars of CORE.md in prompt
data.rules_chars: Max chars of rules in prompt
data.index_chars: Max chars of INDEX.md in prompt
data.note_chars: Max chars when reading a note
data.llm_base_url: LLM base URL for consolidation (e.g. http://localhost:11434/v1)
data.llm_api_key: LLM API key (optional, leave empty for local servers)
data.mcp_url: MCP server URL for HA tool proxy (e.g. http://localhost:8123/api/mcp)
data.mcp_token: MCP server bearer token (HA long-lived access token)
data.mcp_read_only: MCP read-only (hide write/control tools from the model)
data.emby_url: Emby server URL for library search and playback (e.g. http://localhost:8096)
data.emby_api_key: Emby API key (Emby dashboard > API Keys)

no_agent_selected.title: No conversation agent is using Second Brain
no_agent_selected.description:
Second Brain is set up, but no conversation agent has selected it, so the assistant has no access to your notes and cannot remember anything.

Open your conversation agent's options (for example Settings > Devices & services > your LLM integration) and tick **Second Brain** under the control/LLM API setting.

calendars_not_exposed.title: Calendars are not exposed to the assistant
calendars_not_exposed.description:
`get_calendar_events` can only read calendars that are exposed to Assist, and Home Assistant does not expose the calendar domain by default - so appointment questions currently return nothing.

Go to Settings > Voice assistants > Expose and expose the calendars you want the assistant to read.
